data.about: Three reinforced-concrete frames that are the same drawing three times, with one vertical load at midspan each. The title promises different support conditions; the drawings deliver six identical pinned triangles, and the only thing that actually differs is the inclination of the drawn reaction arrows. That inclination is enough. Three forces in equilibrium must be concurrent, so it fixes the height at which the thrust line crosses midspan — and that height decides whether the beam is bending hard, hardly bending at all, or bending the other way. The block carries no scale and no load magnitude, so every answer here is a multiple of F.

steps.caption: page 6 of the sheet: three identical reinforced-concrete frames, each with one vertical load at midspan, and — the title says — three different support conditions. Draw the inner force distribution for each
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: the frame, digitised from the drawing. This is the one block on the whole sheet with NO printed scale, so read the metres as proportions. The legs are 0.72 m wide, the beam 0.75 m deep, the opening 4.56 by 2.45 m
steps.title: The frame

steps.caption: that is the whole tool. The load is vertical at midspan and the two reactions are symmetric, so their lines of action all meet on the midspan axis, at a height fixed by nothing but their inclination
steps.title: Three forces must be concurrent

steps.caption: the thrust line runs straight from each support to that point — and it does not stay in the concrete. The legs are only 0.72 m wide, so an inclined line leaves the inner face almost immediately and spends the rest of its length in the opening
steps.title: Where the load actually goes

steps.caption: the path that does fit: the legs work as columns, and inside the beam a strut fans from the load down to each leg head with a chord closing it. Which chord is the tie depends on the sign of the midspan moment — pink pulls, navy pushes
steps.title: The internal force flow

steps.caption: the midspan moment is zero when tanθ = y_b / a, that is at 46.94°. The sheet’s case b) is drawn at 47.11°, seventeen hundredths of a degree away. a) at 90° gives the beam the whole moment; c) at 62.37° gives it back most of it
steps.title: The number that ties the page together
